# Prio3 test vectors

`vectors_test.go` replays the VDAF draft's published test vectors through this
implementation. Drop the JSON files for `Prio3Count`, `Prio3Sum` and
`Prio3Histogram` in this directory; the test skips when the directory is empty.

## Where to get them

The vectors are generated by the draft's reference implementation and published
alongside it:

- Draft: <https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-irtf-cfrg-vdaf/> — Appendix C
  describes the format, and the vectors themselves live in the draft's source
  repository under `poc/test_vec/`.
- Repository: <https://github.com/cfrg/draft-irtf-cfrg-vdaf>
- ISRG's Rust implementation carries a copy that is convenient to diff against:
  <https://github.com/divviup/libprio-rs> under `src/vdaf/test_vec/`.

**Pin the draft version.** Take all your vectors from one revision and record
which one in this file, because the wire format changed between revisions and
mixing them produces failures that look like implementation bugs.

Vectors from: `draft-irtf-cfrg-vdaf-__` (fill this in)

## Format

Each file is one complete run: a verify key, one or more measurements with the
client randomness that produced them, and every intermediate value in order —
input shares, prep shares, prep messages, output shares, aggregate shares and
the final result. That means you can compare at each protocol step rather than
only at the end, which is the difference between a five-minute fix and an
afternoon.

<!-- STUDY-ONLY-BEGIN -->
## How to use them

Do not start by running the whole harness. Start with one file and one step:

```bash
# 1. Look at the actual JSON before writing any decoding code.
python -m json.tool testdata/Prio3Count_0.json | head -40

# 2. Then iterate on sharding alone.
go test ./internal/vdaf/prio3 -run 'TestDraftTestVectors/Prio3Count' -v
```

The single most common failure is a sharding mismatch caused by the XOF, not by
the sharding logic. Before suspecting `shardEncoded`, confirm
`TestTurboShake128MatchesDraftKAT` in `internal/vdaf/xof` passes — the KAT is a
much smaller haystack.

The second most common failure is the application context (`ctx`) or the
algorithm ID missing from domain separation. Recent drafts bind both into every
derivation; leave either out and every byte differs.

## When they pass

Record it. Put the command and its output in the repository README, and put the
draft revision in the CV bullet:

> Prio3Count/Sum/Histogram implemented from `draft-irtf-cfrg-vdaf-__` and
> validated against the draft's published test vectors.

That sentence is checkable by a stranger in thirty seconds, which is exactly why
it is worth more than any adjective.
